done_when: A job permission card stays bounded across many runs, the reconciler skips cards with nothing pending without loading their payload, a migration shrinks existing oversized cards, and the runtime warns when its main thread is blocked, proven by tests including one that grows a card past 1,000 runs

findings.body: Completed `rerunBarriers` remain unbounded; neither this pruner nor the migration touches them. The production approve-and-run-again path calls `recordRerunConsent` (apps/core/src/application/interactions/job-permission-provider-actions.ts:174), which appends a barrier for each distinct prior run (apps/core/src/application/interactions/job-permission-durability-state.ts:99). Reconciliation only sets `enqueuedAt` (apps/core/src/application/interactions/job-permission-reconciler.ts:529), and removal explicitly preserves enqueued barriers (apps/core/src/application/interactions/job-permission-durability-state.ts:135). Repeated completed handoffs therefore keep enlarging the card, which heartbeats still load and rewrite (apps/core/src/application/interactions/job-permission-provider-actions.ts:544). Safely bound completed rerun state on writes and in the migration, preserving durable enqueue idempotency.
findings.title: Not done: A job permission card stays bounded across many runs, the reconciler skips cards with nothing pending without loading their query

findings.body: The new test supplies 1,001 distinct run IDs, but directly calls the heartbeat reader and `wired.reconcile()` without creating or executing scheduler runs. Delivery settlement and receipts are supplied through SQL at lines 152–163, bypassing the outbound worker rather than faking only the provider edge. The idle-card test likewise calls reconciliation directly. Neither starts the actual five-second loop in apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/runtime-services-permission-card.ts:21, registered by apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/runtime-services.ts:952. Disconnecting scheduler heartbeat wiring or scheduled reconciliation would leave these tests passing. Add the required runtime-entry-point proof for repeated runs and idle-card reconciliation, using real leases, heartbeat scheduling, delivery persistence, and provider-edge fakes.
findings.title: Not done: Grow a permission card past 1,000 runs through the runtime entry point

findings.body: This now meaningfully tests the monitor itself, but it starts that helper directly and observes a mocked logger. It never starts the runtime. Removing the startup registration in apps/core/src/app/index.ts:104 would leave the test passing while eliminating runtime warnings entirely. The required end-to-end proof remains missing: start the real runtime, block its main thread beyond the configured threshold, and verify the emitted warning.
findings.title: Not done: The runtime warns when its main thread is blocked

why: The runtime freezes because one job's permission card grows forever and is reloaded every 5 seconds
